chunks: A number of our companions, from Sahl ibn Ziyad, from Ibn Mahboub, from Al-Hasan ibn al-Sari, from Abu Maryam, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him), who said:

I heard Jabir ibn Abdullah saying: The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) passed by us one day while we were in our gathering, we were in our gathering, and he was upon his she-camel, and that was when he had returned from the Farewell Pilgrimage. He stopped by us, greeted us, and we returned the greeting to him.

Then he said: 'Why do I see that love of the world has overwhelmed many of the people, to the extent that it seems as if death in this world has been decreed for others than them, and as if the truth in this world has been obligated upon others than them, and to the extent that they have not heard or seen the news of the dead before them. Their path is the path of a people traveling; after a short while they will return to their homes, their graves, and their heirs will consume their legacy, thinking that they will be immortal after them. Alas, alas! [A] Will not the latter take lesson from the former? They have indeed been ignorant and forgotten all the advisors in the Book of Allah, and felt safe from the evil of every bad consequence, and did not fear the descent of a calamity and the events of misfortune.'

Goodness is for the one whose fear of Allah, Mighty and Majestic, occupied him from the fear of people. Goodness is for the one whose own fault prevented him from finding faults with the believers from his brothers. Goodness is for the one who humbled himself to Allah, Mighty is His mention, and renounced what Allah had made permissible for him without desiring to deviate from my way of life, and rejected the blossoms of the world without turning away from my Sunnah, and followed the best ones from my progeny after me, and avoided the people of vanity and boasting, and those infatuated with the world, the innovators who oppose my Sunnah, the workers who act upon other than my way.

Goodness is for the one who acquired wealth from the believers without disobedience, so he spent it in non-disobedience, and returned it to the people of poverty. Goodness is for the one whose character was good with people, and who offered them assistance, and turned away from them his evil. Goodness is for the one who spent moderately, and gave the excess, and restrained his speech from vain talk and ugly deeds.
ai.seo_question: What are the characteristics of the blessed ones according to the Prophet's sermon after the Farewell Pilgrimage?
ai.summary: Reported via Jabir ibn Abd Allah, this hadith captures the Prophet’s observation of worldly attachment shortly after the Farewell Pilgrimage, serving as a bridge between his earthly life and the eschatological reality. It emphasizes the Shia ideal of *ittiba'* (following the Prophet and his progeny) as the antidote to vanity, linking spiritual humility with practical ethical conduct in wealth and social interactions.
